title: First Element with Unique Frequency
summary: Given an integer array, identify the first element from the left whose occurrence count is unique.
statement: Given an integer array, identify the first element from the left whose occurrence count is unique. If no such element exists, return -1.
constraints: An element qualifies when its total occurrence count is not shared by any other distinct value.
Return the first qualifying value in array order, or -1 when none qualifies.
hints: The question compares occurrence counts between distinct values, not individual positions.
Count values, then count how many distinct values have each occurrence count.
Scan the original array and return the first value whose count-frequency equals one.
The second map proves uniqueness of the occurrence count, while the final scan enforces leftmost order.
editorial: The second map proves uniqueness of the occurrence count, while the final scan enforces leftmost order.

tests.explanation: Twenty and ten both occur once, while only thirty occurs twice, so thirty is the first qualifying value.
Both distinct values occur once, so neither frequency is unique and the answer is -1.
